original_question: Does every connected d-regular graph admit a signing sigma of its edges such that the signed adjacency matrix has spectral radius at most 2*sqrt(d - 1)?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost exactly: it asks about every connected d-regular graph, a signing/signature of the edges, the signed adjacency matrix, and the sharp bound 2√(d-1) on spectral radius. That is the content of Conjecture 13 in the paper, not the weaker nearby theorem that only controls the largest eigenvalue.
missing_details: The paper works with simple, undirected, unweighted graphs by its global conventions, so that should be stated if the question is to be fully stand-alone.
The signing should be specified as a signature σ:E(G)→{+1,-1}.
The signed adjacency matrix should be explicitly defined, e.g. A_σ(u,v)=σ(uv) when uv∈E(G) and 0 otherwise.
The spectral radius is the spectral radius of this real symmetric signed adjacency matrix, equivalently max{|λ|: λ is an eigenvalue of A_σ}.
The quantifier is unconditional: for every connected d-regular graph G, with no asymptotic qualifier such as 'for sufficiently large d'.

The nearby context matters: Theorem 4 only proves existence of a signature with largest eigenvalue at most 2√(d-1), and Remark 1 explains that this is weaker than bounding the spectral radius. So the refined question should not be rewritten in terms of only the top eigenvalue.
refined_question: For every connected simple undirected d-regular graph G, does there exist a signature σ:E(G)→{+1,-1} such that the signed adjacency matrix A_σ, defined by A_σ(u,v)=σ(uv) if uv∈E(G) and A_σ(u,v)=0 otherwise, has spectral radius ρ(A_σ)≤2√(d-1)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every connected simple undirected d-regular graph G, does there exist a signature σ:E(G)→{+1,-1} such that every eigenvalue of the signed adjacency matrix A_σ lies in the interval [-2√(d-1), 2√(d-1)]?
justification: The draft is aiming at the Bilu-Linial conjecture stated in Section 12 as Conjecture 13. The section first defines signed graphs, signatures, and the signed adjacency matrix, so those definitions are the main stand-alone details missing from the draft. Theorem 3 gives the earlier weaker bound with an absolute constant and logarithmic factor, while Conjecture 13 sharpens this to 2√(d-1). Theorem 4 and Remark 1 are crucial nearby context because they distinguish the proved bound on the largest eigenvalue from the conjectured bound on spectral radius; this confirms that your draft correctly targets spectral radius and should not be relaxed to a statement about only λ1. The alternate formulation is justified by Remark 1, which explicitly describes the conjecture as aiming to place all eigenvalues between -2√(d-1) and 2√(d-1).

citations.label: definition of signed graph, signature, and signed adjacency matrix
